customers: The customers table stores information about customers, including their personal details such as name, email, phone, and city, along with the timestamp when they were created. It contains the following columns: id (unique identifier), name (full name), email (contact email), phone (phone number), city (residence city), and created_at (date of account creation). This table is linked to orders and support_tickets via the customer_id foreign key.
orders: The orders table tracks customer orders, including details such as the order date, status, total amount, and shipping city. It contains the following columns: id (unique order identifier), customer_id (foreign key to customers), order_date (timestamp of order placement), status (current order status), total_amount (total value of the order), and shipping_city (city for delivery). This table is linked to order_items via order_id and to customers via customer_id.
support_tickets: The support_tickets table records customer support interactions, including the subject, status, priority, and timestamps for creation and resolution. It contains the following columns: id (unique ticket identifier), customer_id (foreign key to customers), employee_id (foreign key to employees), subject (summary of the issue), status (current ticket status), priority (severity level), created_at (timestamp of ticket creation), and resolved_at (timestamp of resolution). This table is linked to customers and employees via their respective foreign keys.
order_items: The order_items table lists individual products included in an order, including the product ID, quantity, and unit price. It contains the following columns: id (unique item identifier), order_id (foreign key to orders), product_id (identifier for the product), quantity (number of units), and unit_price (price per unit). This table is linked to orders via order_id and to products (not explicitly listed in the schema) via product_id.
employees: The employees table stores information about staff members, including their name, email, department, role, city, and hire date. It contains the following columns: id (unique employee identifier), name (full name), email (work email), department (work department), role (job title), city (residence city), and hire_date (date of employment start). This table is linked to support_tickets via the employee_id foreign key.
products: The products table stores information about individual items available for sale. Each record represents a distinct product with a unique identifier (id), a human-readable name (name), a category (category) that classifies the product type, a monetary value (price), a count of available units (stock_quantity), and a timestamp (created_at) indicating when the product was first recorded in the system. This table is used to look up product details, categorize inventory, track availability, and audit creation dates for sales and inventory management purposes.
